notes.text: Chris Tanev has not dressed for the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Darren Raddysh has taken his spot beside Jake McCabe. That pair has had 50% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 111:54 together, up from 36% with Tanev.
Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Gavin McKenna has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews.
Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Dakota Mermis has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
John Tavares is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Chris Tanev is expected back after missing 9 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Vinni Lettieri was added to the roster on Oct 19 and has played beside Colton Sissons and Gavin McKenna.
Dakota Mermis was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 15 games, up from 6% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Filip Chytil is on injured reserve (upper body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Max Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 15 games, up from 4% last season.

VAN.head: The Canucks face a real test
VAN.body: Toronto has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and gets Tanev back, but they will be without Marchenko, and Vancouver has home-ice advantage. The Canucks’ best way through is a power play that gets going.

TOR.head: The matchup suits the Maple Leafs

story.head: Blueger returns to Vancouver
paras: The Maple Leafs (7-6-2) lost 5-4 to Seattle on Wednesday, and the Canucks (3-11-1) lost 3-2 to San Jose on Thursday. Going in, the Maple Leafs are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 13th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Maple Leafs’ record (.533) is about what their chances are worth. The Canucks have played better than their record (.233) says: their chances are worth about .299, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Canucks (32nd) and the Maple Leafs (30th) both have had shaky goaltending. The Leafs get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (30th). Toronto has scored 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league. As for the Canucks, they pick their shots (lowest). They also have a leaky penalty kill (32nd), so the Maple Leafs’ power play (8th) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. Vancouver has allowed 4.53 goals a game, the most in the league. The Canucks roll four lines, but the Maple Leafs lean on their top six.

Auston Matthews (10 G / 13 A / 23 P in 15 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is fourth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. William Nylander (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 15 GP) is next in line, with four goals in six games against Vancouver since 2023-24. For the Canucks, Elias Pettersson (#40) (4 G / 12 A / 16 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Jonathan Lekkerimäki (6 G / 6 A / 12 P in 15 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Anthony Stolarz (4-1-0 / .906 SV% in 5 GS) is expected to start for Toronto, and Leevi Meriläinen (2-4-1 / .898 SV% in 8 GS) for Vancouver.
At home, Manny Malhotra likes to send Cotter, Sasson and Bains out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Groulx, Sissons and Lettieri.

items.text: Teddy Blueger faces Vancouver for the first time since leaving.

The Maple Leafs are newly without Kirill Marchenko and Nick Blankenburg, and have been without John Tavares since Oct 15. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Islanders are missing more right now.
The Canucks are newly without Filip Chytil, and have had to make do without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
Jonathan Lekkerimäki has six goals on chances worth about 2.8 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
